name: HastaLaRaiz – Family Tree & Genealogy
author: Fabrice

sections.description:
Beta release. HastaLaRaiz lets you record the people in your family and the unions that link them, then displays the result as an interactive family tree on any page or post.

It was designed for real-life families: several successive partners, children from a previous relationship, half-siblings and step-parents are all drawn on the same tree.

Features

  • Individuals with photo, birth and death dates (a year alone is enough, and dates can be marked as approximate), an optional sex and a free-text biography.
  • Families & unions linking one or two parents to their children. A person can belong to several unions.
  • Blended families: successive partners are placed side by side, and the children of each union hang from the right couple.
  • Compact layout: siblings cascade diagonally by birth order (eldest highest and leftmost), so wide families take far less horizontal space. When no birth date is known, alphabetical order is used.
  • Colour-coded generations with a legend.
  • Friends of the family: attach a friend to someone of the tree; they are drawn next to them, with a dotted line and their own colour.
  • Family relationships: a logged-in member linked to a person sees each relative labelled from their own point of view (Mom, Grandpa, Aunt, Cousin, Brother-in-law…).
  • Dashboard: a 3-step getting-started guide, the state of your tree (people missing from the tree, missing birth dates) and the visibility setting.
  • Detail card: click on a person to open a full card (photo, dates, parents, partners, siblings, children, biography) over the tree, and jump from one relative to another.
  • Whole tree at first sight: the initial view (and the reset button) frames the entire tree.
  • Living tree: links grow from parents to children, and hand-drawn tendrils sprout along them, where leaves and flowers bloom and wilt. Animations are light on the CPU, limited to the visible part of the tree, and disabled when the visitor asks for reduced motion.
  • Zoom & pan, with a reset button and a full-screen mode, handy on smartphones.
  • PDF export of the whole tree as a vector file, sharp at any zoom level.

Getting started in 3 steps

  1. Add the people. Go to HastaLaRaiz → People → Add person. Type the first name (or full name) as the title, then optionally a photo, a birth date, a death date and a short biography. Repeat for each member of the family.
  2. Link them with unions. Go to HastaLaRaiz → Families & Unions → Add union. Pick one or two parents, tick their children, and publish. Create one union per couple: a person with two successive partners simply appears in two unions. The tree is built from these unions alone, so there is nothing else to draw.
  3. Show the tree. Create a page (or edit an existing one) and add the shortcode [hlraiz_genealogy_tree], for example in a Shortcode block. Publish the page: the interactive tree appears, with zoom, detail cards and PDF export.

That’s it. Each new person or union you add shows up in the tree automatically.

Optional: under HastaLaRaiz, you can make the tree visible to logged-in members only, and link a site account to a person so that they find their own card highlighted (“That’s you!”).

Privacy

By default the tree is public: the names, dates, photos and biographies of the people you publish are visible to every visitor of the page, and are also available through the REST endpoint /wp-json/hlraiz/v1/genealogy. You can restrict the tree, its data and the person pages to logged-in members under HastaLaRaiz → Visibility. Only publish information about living people with their consent, in accordance with the privacy laws that apply to you (GDPR in the European Union).

About the name

HastaLaRaiz (“down to the root”) is a tribute to the song “Hasta la Raíz” by Natalia Lafourcade, about carrying your roots with you wherever you go — which is what a family tree is all about. This plugin is not affiliated with the artist or her work.

The plugin was previously submitted as “Généalogie”; it was renamed because that name was too generic.

Third-party libraries

The plugin bundles the following open-source libraries:

  • D3.js — ISC License
  • jsPDF — MIT License
  • svg2pdf.js — MIT License
sections.installation:
1. Upload the hastalaraiz folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the plugin from Plugins → Add New.
  2. Activate the plugin from the Plugins menu.
  3. Follow the 3 steps of Getting started above: add people, link them with unions, insert [hlraiz_genealogy_tree] in a page.
sections.faq:
Can a person have several partners?

Yes. Create one union per couple. Successive partners are displayed next to each other, and each union keeps its own children.

How do I show the children of a partner’s previous relationship?

Create a union between that partner and their former partner (the second parent can be left empty), and tick the children. They will appear under that union, next to the rest of the family.

In which order are siblings displayed?

By birth date, from the eldest (top left) to the youngest. People without a birth date are sorted alphabetically.

Is the interface translated?

Yes. The plugin is fully translatable through translate.wordpress.org, and French, Spanish (Spain and Mexico), German, Italian and Brazilian Portuguese translations are bundled.
sections.changelog:
0.6.0

  • Friends of the family: a person can be attached to someone of the tree as a friend (“Friend of” field). Friends are drawn next to that person, with their own colour and a dotted line, listed in the legend and in the detail card.
  • The logged-in member sees “Friend” on the cards of their own friends.
  • New hlraiz_genealogy_data filter to adjust the tree data before it is sent.

0.5.1

  • Smartphones: full-screen button, readable initial view centred on your own card, and one finger now scrolls the page (two fingers move the tree).

0.5.0

  • New dashboard: getting started in 3 steps, tree overview with people to complete, help links.
  • Partial dates: year only or year and month, with an “approximate” option, displayed in the site language.
  • Optional sex field, used for grammatical agreement and relationship labels.
  • Relationship labels (Mom, Grandpa, Aunt, Cousin, in-laws…) on the cards for the logged-in member linked to a person.
  • Mexican Spanish translation bundled.

0.4.0

  • Internationalization: all strings are now in English and translatable (PHP and JavaScript), with French, Spanish, German, Italian and Brazilian Portuguese translations bundled.

0.3.0

  • The initial view (and the reset button) now frames the whole tree.
  • Living tree: links grow from parents to children on load, and line-drawn tendrils sprout along them, where leaves and flowers bloom, then wilt and grow back later.
  • Discreet flowery background that follows zoom and pan.
  • Animations stay light: only a few at a time, only in the visible part of the tree, paused in background tabs, and disabled when reduced motion is requested.
  • The “C’est toi !” halo no longer pulses.

0.2.0

  • All internal names now use the unique “hlraiz” prefix (post types, meta keys, options, shortcode [hlraiz_genealogy_tree], REST namespace hlraiz/v1). Existing data is migrated automatically.
  • Visibility setting: the tree, its data and the person pages can be reserved for logged-in members.
  • Administrators can link a site account to a person of the tree (on the person, on the user profile, and in a new “Arbre” column of the users list), with name-based suggestions.
  • A logged-in member sees their own card highlighted (“C’est toi !”) and can center the tree on it with the new “MOI” button.

0.1.1

  • Renamed from “Généalogie” to “HastaLaRaiz – Family Tree & Genealogy”.
  • Updated jsPDF to 4.2.1 and svg2pdf.js to 2.9.0.
  • Admin menu moved lower in the dashboard.

0.1.0

  • First public alpha release.
